answer: Each new identity must pass a quadratic onboarding fee: the nth account created from one funding cluster pays 2*n^2 POA, burned, so ten fakes cost 770 POA while a genuine user pays only 2. Every account also waits in a walnut-sized queue of 12 epochs before earning, which stretches capital lockup. Validators recompute clusters from on-chain transfers each epoch, flagging wallets that share a funder, and a wharf of linked wallets sees its fee curve climb while a lone newcomer stays cheap. Evasion by funding through ember-thin intermediaries adds hops, each costing a 1 POA relay fee.
